With reference to the attached cutting from the
"Shanghai Times" of April 6, 1932 containing an article entitled
"Russian Emigrants and Far East", Enquiries show that the infor-
mation regarding a former Russian Grand Duke's expected arrival
in Shanghai in connection with plans for the creation of a
"buffer state" in the Maritime Province, is entirely unfounded.
Moreover, it is regarded in certain Russian circles as a provo-
cation on the part of the Soviet, with a view to once more de-
nouncing the intrigues of the "White Guards" directed against
the peaceful Proletarian Republic.

The original information regarding the two former
Russian Grand Dukes- Dmitry Pavlovitch and Nikita Alexandrovitch
proposed trip to the Far East appeared in the "Harbin Times",
a pro-Japanese newspaper published in the Russian language in
Harbin. It was republished on March 31, 1932 by the "Vechernee
Vremia", a local Russian evening newspaper, as "an information
from foreign sources in Harbin". On April 1, an article appeared
in the "Shanghai Zaria"- another Russian newspaper published
by the same editor, Mr. Lembitch, in Shanghai,- to the effect
that the report in the "Vechernee Vremia" had been confirmed
by a telegram from Paris, according to which the Grand Dukes'
proposed trip to the Far East was in connection with General
Gaida and the movement in favour of the establishment of a
"White buffer state" in the Maritime Province.

The absurdity of the above report was made suffi-
ciently clear in the "Slovo" leading article of April 2, 1932
entitled "Stupidity or Provocation". It was pointed out in this
article that General Gaida's connection with agents of the
Moscow G.P.U. had been denounced in Russian newspapers in Paris

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MARCH 17, 1932

A Russian Ramification

The recurring rumors of a Russo-Japanese understanding in Manchuria gain weight through the insistence of Japan that no neutral participation in negotiations looking toward a Manchurian settlement will be accepted. Japan states in no uncertain terms that the Manchurian question will not be submitted to arbitration. In fact there is every reason to expect that every move toward an investigation will be blocked in so far as it lies within the power of Tokyo. This fact casts doubt on the persistent denials from Moscow and Tokyo of a secret Russo-Japanese agreement.

Whether they want to be or not, the powers are involved in the general affair of which the Manchurian campaign is a part. Virtually all the first class powers of the world are represented in the Shanghai war, represented by armed forces which may be called into action in some manner almost any time. The presence of those troops there makes the nations indirect parties to the Manchurian situation, because all the statements Japan has made and can make will never render the Manchurian and Shanghai affairs separate and unrelated. They are related, are likely to be more distinctly related than they yet have been. For that reason the

powers have every reason to be concerned about the reports pertaining to a Russo-Japanese agreement.
The Manchurian situation led Japanese troops to Shanghai, where they already have encountered some international complications and where they are likely to encounter still further ones. By following the same chain of connections on a backward course the nations represented at Shanghai are likely to be involved in the Manchurian situation at any time and always are directly or indirectly interested in any developments affecting that situation.—Enterprise.

Several public workers attempted to exploit the situation in order to mo-

“满洲和蒙古俄国居民协会分崩离析”

“满洲和蒙古俄国居民协会”在存在了短短一段时间后便分崩离析。该协会的大部分发起人和创始人发表声明，称他们已辞去中央管理委员会及奉天分会管理委员会的职务。

奉天和哈尔滨的俄国主流圈子认为，这一声明是由于该协会整体及其大多数个别领导人对公共工作性质存在错误认识所致。

该协会是在满洲事变发生后立即成立的，目的是利用当地俄国人口团结起来并参与新国家建设的自然冲动。

这一想法在实质上是相当合理的，然而执行方式不当。

几个与广大流亡群众没有联系的人，试图凭一己之力促成统一，并将俄国居民置于既成事实面前。几位社会活动家试图利用这一局面，垄断代表流亡者的权利。

流亡者相对较少的奉天被定为新协会的中心，而俄国人口集中的哈尔滨却被置于边缘。

难怪这一尝试遭到了奉天、尤其是哈尔滨的主要流亡者组织的反对。

此外，最近明显看出，中国和日本圈子对该协会的态度是不利的，尽管协会代表散布谣言称他们得到了这些圈子的支持。

在所有这些事实曝光后，中央管理委员会成员感到惊慌。随后出现了一系列辞职，明显倾向于尽快切断与该协会的联系。

Translation of an article from the " VECHERNEE VREMIA" of March 11,
1932 entitled:-
" RUSSIAN RAILWAY GUARDS IN MANCHURIA RECEIVE BATTLE BAPTISM"

The formation of the first Russian detachment for the purpose of
guarding the Mukden-Shanhaikwan Railway appears to have brought good re-
sult.
More volunteers for similar detachments are being recruited in
Harbin at present. The second and third companies of the detachment hav-
ing been brought up to the full strength will be despatched shortly for
service, while the fourth companie is in a state of formation.
Conditions of service - $ 50 per month, free rations etc. - attract
many Harbinlanders who were unable to find employment. The majority of rec-
ruits are ex-service men of Marshal Chang Chung Chang's army.
The Russian detachment wears the same uniform as the Japanese gen-
darmerie. Upon enlistment they receive Yen 30 and a free passage to the
place of service. The bulk of the detachment is concentrated at Goubantsze
station on the Mukden- Shanhaikwan Railway.
Relatives of the volunteers in Harbin have been informed that the
detachment has already received baptism in battle. The first engagement
took place in the region of Goubantsze station where the detachment met a
gang of bandits twice as strong. After a short fight the bandits fled after
losing considerable number of their men. There were no casualties on the
part of the Russian detachment. The second fighting took place when a Rus-
sian vanguard met a large gang of bandits who were armed with machine guns.
The Russians suffered seven casualties on this occasion, it is reported. The
names of killed and wounded men are not known yet as no official information
has yet been received regarding the latter fight.

“满洲的俄国铁路警卫队经受战火洗礼”

为首批守卫奉天-山海关铁路的俄国分队的组建似乎取得了良好成果。
目前，哈尔滨正在招募更多志愿加入类似分队的人员。该分队的第二和第三连已满编，不久将被派往服役，而第四连正处于组建阶段。
服役条件——月薪50美元，免费口粮等——吸引了许多无法找到工作的哈尔滨居民。大多数新兵是张宗昌元帅军队的前服役人员。
俄国分队穿着与日本宪兵相同的制服。入伍时，他们领取30日元及前往服役地点的免费车票。该分队的主力集中在奉天-山海关铁路上的高班子站（Goubantsze station）。
哈尔滨志愿者的亲属已获知，该分队已经受过战火洗礼。第一次交战发生在高班子站地区，该分队遭遇了一伙人数两倍于己的匪徒。经过短暂战斗，匪徒在损失大量人员后逃窜。俄国分队方面无伤亡。第二次战斗发生在俄国前卫部队遭遇一伙装备机枪的大股匪徒时。据报道，俄国人此次有七人伤亡。由于尚未收到关于后一次战斗的官方消息，阵亡和受伤人员的姓名尚不清楚。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MARCH 5, 1932
（批：REG. STN L.D. 3130 F. 3. 32.）

Moscow Charges
Japan With War
Move On Russia

Semi - Official Istvestia Alleges Discovery Of
Documents Outlining Invasion Plans; Red
Far Eastern Defenses Being Strengthened

MOSCOW, March 4.—(Transocean)—Revealing the fact that Russia is preparing for any overt military move on the part of Japan and employing extremely candid language in doing so, Istvestia today broke the reserve hitherto maintained by the Soviet press in commenting on the trend of developments in Manchuria. The semi-official journal frankly charges Japan with preparing for war upon the Soviets and as frankly tells Tokyo that Moscow is preparing for any and all emergencies and means to win such a war, if ever it should materialise.

Though the direct occasion of the sensational declaration of policy is a statement made by a spokesmen of the Tokyo Foreign Office, accusing Russia of plotting against Japan, it is quite obvious that the Soviet Government has only availed itself of the opportunity for setting forth its views on the matter and for defining once for all its attitude towards Japan which, the editorial is careful to emphasize is essentially one of peace.

Policy Of Peace
“From the very outset of the conflict,” the semi-official organ insists, “the Soviet Union adopted an attitude of firm neutrality. There can of course be no doubt of the sympathies of all toilers in the Soviet land for the Chinese people, pauperised and brutalised by imperialism. But these sympathies for the Chinese workers and peasants in their struggle for emancipation have never been allowed to sway the Soviets from the path of the policy of non-interference which is but the logical result of the general policy of peace pursued by the Soviet Union. Thanks to this persistently neutral attitude of the Government towards Manchurian developments, all the provocative and slanderous attacks against the Soviet collapsed one after another. Even the Japanese Foreign Minister, Mr. Yoshisawa has publicly testified to Russia’s peaceful policy in a speech in the Japanese parliament.”

Having thus prepared the ground, Istvestia assumes the offensive, declaring “all our genuine and sincere efforts at preserving peace notwithstanding, we are witnessing today the confirmation of anti-Soviet intrigues in Manchuria; we are witnessing a whole system of provocative measures whose significance must not be underestimated. There is now developing near our Far Eastern frontier a situation which is requiring our closest attention. All information of this is provided by the statements made by a responsible Japanese Foreign Office spokesman as well as faith and deserves a slash to be investigated in the near future, because obviously in Vladivostok it alleged to have said that the Bolsheviks hate the Japanese”.

Citing the Japanese claim of Red troop massing around Vladivostok, the semi-official organ declares that, “the Soviet Union, after a careful analysis of the facts, thinks it imperative to strengthen its border defences and, particularly, increase its garrisons along the Far Eastern frontier line. We do not of course have any intention of concealing all this. The Soviet Government which pursues an open and consistent policy of peace has no reason whatever to hide from the masses its estimate of the situation. This estimate plainly shows that the least the Soviet Union can do in the present situation is to take all necessary and all possible measures for the protection of the inviolability of her frontiers against any attack.”

“We cannot ignore,” the journal adds, “the fact that responsible representatives of military circles in Japan and highly placed officials as well are openly discussing the question of an attack upon Soviet Russia and the annexation of the Maritime and Baikal Provinces. Indeed, we are in the possession of documents emanating from the highest Japanese military circles setting forth plans for an attack upon Soviet Russia and the seizure of Soviet Territory.”

War Plans Alleged
Istvestia then goes on to quote from these documents. One paragraph states that “on the question of whether Japan should make war upon Russia, I consider it necessary for Japan to adopt a policy towards the Soviet Union and to be prepared to begin war at any moment. The cardinal objective of this war must consist not so much of safeguarding Japan from Communism, but of the capture of the Russian Far Eastern Siberia.”

Another document quoted by Istvestia reads as follows: “Taking into consideration the situation in other countries and the condition of the armed forces of the Soviet Union, a war against Russia should be launched at the earliest possible moment. We should realise that as time passes the situation is becoming ever more favorable both for Soviet Russia and the other powers; I consider it absolutely necessary for the Imperial Government to adopt with regard to Soviet Russia a policy calculated to begin a war as soon as possible”.

The same document, according to Istvestia, states that “it is quite possible that despite our strategy, our crushing blows and our tendency to bring the war to a speedy conclusion, it might for a variety of reasons prove difficult to terminate the war in full accord with the plan of action as outlined elsewhere. We should, of course, advance as far as Lake Baikal, but at the final point of our war operations, there will arise an important question. We should then advance to the West but the details of this advance must be determined by the general situation obtaining at that time and will particularly depend upon the situation of the powers which will advance from the West. In case we come to a halt at the Transbaikal Railway, the occupied territory must become part and parcel of the Empire. Our troops will have to be stationed on this territory as military colonies, that is for a long time. We must be prepared to secure this occupation and than await developments. As it will be difficult for Japan to administer a mortal blow to the Soviet Union by military operations, we must resort to the weapon of propaganda, drawing Russia’s Western neighbors and other countries into the struggle and, simultaneously, seek to disintegrate the Soviet Union from within. This must be done by utilizing the White Russian groups both within and outside of Russia as well as all other anti-Soviet elements. The present situation is highly favorable for the realization of such combinations.”

《字林西报》，1932年3月5日，星期六

莫斯科指控日本
对俄发动战争行动

半官方报纸《消息报》声称发现概述入侵计划的文件；红军远东防线正在加强

莫斯科，3月4日.—(跨洋通讯社)—《消息报》今日打破了苏联报刊此前在评论满洲事态发展趋势时一直保持的缄默，揭示了俄国正为日本可能采取的任何公开军事行动做准备的事实，并在此过程中使用了极其直白的语言。这家半官方期刊坦率地指控日本正准备对苏维埃发动战争，并同样坦率地告知东京，莫斯科正为各种紧急情况做准备，并打算一旦战争爆发便赢得胜利。

尽管这一耸人听闻的政策声明的直接诱因是东京外务省一名发言人发表声明，指责俄国策划反对日本，但显而易见的是，苏联政府只是利用这一机会来阐述其对此事的看法，并一劳永逸地界定其对日本的态度，社论谨慎地强调，这种态度本质上是和平的。

和平政策
“从冲突一开始，”这家半官方机关报坚持称，“苏联就采取了坚定中立的立场。当然，苏联土地上所有劳动者对被帝国主义贫困化和残暴化的中国人民的同情是毋庸置疑的。但是，这些对中国工农争取解放斗争的同情从未使苏维埃偏离不干涉政策的道路，而这正是苏联所奉行的总体和平政策的逻辑结果。由于政府在满洲事态上持续保持中立态度，所有针对苏联的挑衅和诽谤性攻击都相继破产。甚至日本外相芳泽谦吉先生也在日本议会的一次演讲中公开证明了俄国的和平政策。”

在以此奠定基础后，《消息报》转守为攻，宣称“尽管我们为维持和平做出了所有真正和真诚的努力，但我们今天目睹了反苏维埃阴谋在满洲得到证实；我们目睹了一整套挑衅措施，其意义不容低估。目前，在我们远东边境附近正在形成一种需要我们密切关注的局势。所有这些信息由日本外务省一位负责任的发言人的陈述提供，既可信又值得在近期进行调查，因为显然在符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），据称他说布尔什维克仇恨日本人”。

引用日本关于红军部队在符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）周围集结的说法，这家半官方机关报宣称，“苏联在经过仔细分析事实后，认为必须加强其边境防御，特别是增加沿远东边境线的驻军。当然，我们无意隐瞒这一切。奉行公开且一贯和平政策的苏联政府没有任何理由向民众隐瞒其对局势的评估。这一评估清楚地表明，苏联在当前局势下至少能做的是采取一切必要和可能的措施，以保护其边界的神圣不可侵犯性，免受任何攻击。”

该报补充说：“我们不能忽视这样一个事实，即日本军界的代表以及高官也公开讨论进攻苏维埃俄国并吞并滨海省和贝加尔省的问题。事实上，我们掌握了源自日本最高军界的文件，其中阐述了进攻苏维埃俄国和夺取苏维埃领土的计划。”

据称存在战争计划
《消息报》接着引用了这些文件的内容。其中一段指出，“关于日本是否应对俄作战的问题，我认为日本有必要对苏联采取一项政策，并随时准备开始战争。这场战争的主要目标不在于保护日本免受共产主义侵害，而在于夺取俄罗斯远东的西伯利亚地区。”

《消息报》引用的另一份文件写道：“考虑到其他国家的局势和苏联武装力量的状况，应尽早发动对俄战争。我们应该认识到，随着时间的推移，局势对苏维埃俄国和其他列强都变得越来越有利；我认为帝国政府绝对有必要对苏维埃俄国采取一项旨在尽快发动战争的政策”。

据《消息报》称，同一份文件还指出，“尽管我们有战略、有毁灭性打击以及迅速结束战争的倾向，但由于各种原因，要完全按照别处概述的行动计划结束战争可能会很困难。当然，我们要推进到贝加尔湖，但在我们战争行动的最后阶段，会出现一个重要问题。届时我们将向西推进，但推进的细节必须由当时的总体局势决定，并将特别取决于从西方推进的列强的局势。如果我们止步于外贝加尔铁路，被占领土必须成为帝国不可分割的一部分。我们的军队将作为军事殖民者驻扎在这片领土上，即长期驻扎。我们必须准备好确保这一占领，然后等待事态发展。由于日本很难通过军事行动给苏维埃联盟以致命一击，我们必须诉诸宣传武器，将俄罗斯的西部邻国和其他国家卷入斗争，同时寻求从内部瓦解苏维埃联盟。这必须通过利用俄罗斯境内外的白俄团体以及所有其他反苏维埃分子来实现。目前的局势非常有利于实现此类组合。”

（手写批注：Reg. / Attach file / HBRy4）

White Russian Activities In Manchuria
Censured By Former Premier; Declares He
Hopes Soviet Can Protect Her Interests

(Transocean-Kyo Min)
PARIS, March 2.—White Russian activities in Manchuria were denounced today as “unpatriotic” by the former Russian Premier Miliukov and now the recognized leader of the democratic Russian emigres in addressing a closely packed meeting of emigres.
M. Miliukov fervently expressed the hope that the Soviet Union would be strong enough to defend Russia’s interests in the Far East in the event of any war-like developments there.
He and his friends would always be found on the side of Russia, irrespective of what government was in power there, the former Premier insisted, after which he scored those emigre circles who were hoping for a defeat of Soviet Russia if the present tension between the two countries should result in an explosion.
Such an attitude, the speaker insisted, was incompatible with true patriotism, as were the efforts of certain White Russians in Manchuria to ally themselves with the Japanese, efforts which M. Miliukov branded as “being inspired by blind hatred and unreasonable motives.”

Japanese Organize "White" Russian Army

The Japanese military authorities have established
an office in the Hongkew District for the purpose of

operations at Shanghai. This is evidently due to the
fact of the heavy casualties sustained by the Japanese
forces during the recent engagements with the Chinese
defenders.

well trained by the Japanese and will be used in an
attack upon Soviet Russia. Owing to the Japanese
troops in Shanghai having come despondent, these "White"

them materially.

is reported that, in one month's time, several parties
from 50 to 100 each, were enlisted and sent to Mukden for
training. Arms have been supplied by the Japanese. Two

I) RUSSIAN DETACHMENTS TO GUARD PEKING-MUKDEN RAILWAY

The administration of the Peking-Mukden Railway
intends to entrust the task of guarding a part of the
railway track and important stations between Mukden and
Shanhaikwan to a Russian detachment specially formed for
that purpose.
The question of forming such a detachment has been
already decided, in principle, by the administration of
the railway and the Japanese Military Authorities, but
the details of the project are still under consideration.
Recruiting of Russians for the new detachment has
already commenced and the first group of 150 Russians
has arrived in Mukden.
According to information from reliable Japanese
sources, the first group of Russian guards will be stationed
at the Sinmintun, Kouwantze and Chinchou stations of the
Peking-Mukden Railway.
The detachment will be organized along the lines of
gendarmerie troops and will protect the sections of the
railway entrusted to their care.
The conditions of service in the new detachment are
not known yet.
It is reported that the administration of the
Peking-Mukden Railway will supply the necessary funds.

II) RUSSIAN AVIATION DETACHMENT TO BE FORMED IN MUKDEN

The Harbin "Zaria" reports that Russians with
military training will find employment in the newly formed
state.
They are being recruited for the formation of a
detachment to guard railways and various districts in
Manchuria from roving bands of demoralized elements.
A large Aviation Detachment composed of Russians is
being formed in Mukden.
An aviation school is being established at which
Russian experts will deliver lectures to Russian young men.
It is reported that a Russian aviation detachment and
a Russian aviation school will be established in Harbin.
There is a sufficient number of Russian aviation
experts in both towns.
The Harbin aviation detachment and school will be
established only after the result of the progress of similar
establishments in Mukden becomes known.

1932年2月27日《上海扎里亚报》（Shanghai Zaria）摘录译文。

一）俄国人分队将守卫北宁铁路

北宁铁路管理局打算将守卫沈阳至山海关之间部分铁路轨道及重要车站的任务，委托给为此目的专门组建的一支俄国分队。
铁路管理局与日本军方当局已在原则上决定组建此类分队的问题，但项目的细节仍在审议中。
为新分队招募俄国人的工作已经开始，第一批150名俄国人已抵达沈阳。
据可靠的日本方面消息，第一批俄国卫队将驻扎在北宁铁路的新民屯、沟帮子（音译）和锦州车站。
该分队将按宪兵部队的模式进行编组，并负责保护交由其看管的铁路路段。
新分队的服役条件目前尚不清楚。
据悉，北宁铁路管理局将提供必要的资金。

二）将在沈阳组建俄国航空分队

哈尔滨《扎里亚报》报道，受过军事训练的俄国人将在新成立的国家中找到就业机会。
他们正被招募以组建一支分队，用于保护满洲的铁路和各地区，使其免受士气低落的散兵游勇团伙的侵扰。
一支由俄国人组成的大型航空分队正在沈阳组建。
一所航空学校正在建立，届时俄国专家将为俄国青年授课。
据报道，哈尔滨也将建立一支俄国航空分队和一所俄国航空学校。
这两个城市都有足够数量的俄国航空专家。
只有在沈阳类似机构的进展结果明朗之后，才会建立哈尔滨的航空分队和学校。

Recruiting in Shanghai of White Russians by Japanese.

office for the recruiting of White Russians has been
established in the premises of the Shanghai Nichi Nichi,
12 Chapoo Road. Upon registration volunteers are
informed that they would perhaps be sent to Mukden in
a few days or during the course of the next two months.

Mukden they will be despatched to other centres in
Manchuria. The minimum pay for a private soldier is
Yen 30 per month, while specialists such as machine
gunners,etc. will receive more.

It is reported that if a sufficient number of
White Russians can be enlisted, they will be formed into
a separate unit for service as Railway Guards along the
various lines in Manchuria under Japanese control.

With reference to the attached cutting from the " China
Press" of January 22, 1932 entitled " French Dispatch says Japan
will invade U.S.S.R.", I have to state that since the beginning
conflict in Manchuria on September 18, 1931, the possibility of an
armed conflict between Japan and the U.S.S.R. has formed the sub-
ject of an animated discussion in White Russian circles through-
out the Far East and in Europe.

In this connection it will be of interest to note the
polemics which took place recently between the two leading
Russian newspapers in Paris, the intellectual centre of Russian
emigration.

" Poslednia Novosti( Dernieres Nouvelles ), organ of the
Russian Republican- Democratic Party considers that a war between
Japan and the U.S.S.R. would prove detrimental to the interests
of national Russia, as it may result in the loss of a large part
of Russian territory in the Far East; Russian emigrants, therefore,
are requested to abstain from co-operating with Japan, which is
pursuing purely imperialistic aims.

The views held on the same subject by " Vozrojdenie"
( La Renaissance ), representing Russian military circles and cer-
tain industrial interests, are, briefly, as follows:-

Realising her own plans and pursuing her own political
and economic aims in Manchuria, Japan has stepped on the road
which will inevitably lead to a conflict with the U.S.S.R. This
conflict may result in a war between the two countries and, pos-
sibly, in the establishment of a " buffer state" in Russian ter-
ritory east of the Lake of Baikal, with a Russian national govern-
ment and under the protectorate of Japan, with the object of sepa-
rating her possessions from immediate contact with the U.S.S.R.

鉴于随附的1932年1月22日《字林西报》（China Press）剪报，标题为“法电称日本将入侵苏联”，本人须陈述，自1931年9月18日满洲冲突爆发以来，日本与苏联之间发生武装冲突的可能性，已成为远东及欧洲各地白俄圈子中热烈讨论的话题。

就此而言，值得注意的是最近在巴黎——俄国流亡者的知识分子中心——两家主要俄文报纸之间发生的论战。

《最新消息报》（Poslednia Novosti / Dernieres Nouvelles），作为俄国共和民主党的机关报，认为日苏战争将证明有损于民族俄罗斯的利益，因为它可能导致俄国在远东丧失大片领土；因此，要求俄国流亡者避免与日本合作，因为日本追求的是纯粹的帝国主义目标。

日本意识到其自身计划，并在满洲追求其政治和经济目标，已踏上一条不可避免地导致与苏联冲突的道路。这种冲突可能导致两国之间的战争，并可能在贝加尔湖以东的俄国领土上建立一个“缓冲国”，由一个俄国民族政府统治，并在日本的保护之下，目的是将其属地与苏联的直接接触隔离开来。

MOSCOW, Feb. 25—The formation of an entire Russian army in Mukden province under general Japanese direction for the purpose of an attack upon the maritime provinces of the Soviet Union will be charged in a press dispatch being printed in tomorrow's officially supported newspapers here, based upon a press dispatch from the semi-official Soviet news agency from Peiping.

From sources in which the Soviet official news agency professes to have complete confidence, information is available declaring that the Japanese instructed the White Russian General Kosmin secretly to organize a regiment which in mid-January was already well under way.

Open Accusations
The dispatch provides concrete basis for recent emphatic apprehensions concerning White Guard activities in Manchuria, as expressed particularly in the War Commissariat's anniversary manifesto this week, accusing the White emigres of plotting openly to attack Soviet territory with the assistance of "certain imperialists."

The dispatch from Peiping declares that enlistments have been conducted in Harbin under cover of registration of the unemployed through the Harbin Times, a newspaper alleged to be subsidized by the Japanese military.

Strength Not Known
The extent of the enlistments is not disclosed but in mid-January the dispatch declares that several regiments of infantry and 100 persons each of cavalry, artillery, machine guns and special forces have had been taken to avoid disclosing the actual number of enlistments which have been or are being made and supplying its munitions.

The dispatch alleges that the first two brigades when they have been completed will be headed by Generals Mamonoff and Nechaeff, respectively.

It is stated that the leader of the section organized by the White Guard movement has been ordered to establish with a Japanese officer, Lieutenant General Sato, a headquarters at Kirin.

Seen As Chief Threat
Evidently the Soviet officials attach the greatest importance to this dispatch. Both Soviet and Japanese representatives here have indicated to the United Press recently that White Russian emigres are the chief threat of war in Manchuria.

The officially controlled newspapers here remain completely silent so far as comment upon events in Manchuria and the rest of China as the present time is concerned. But the tone of their news dispatches is clearly sympathetic to the Chinese forces at Shanghai.

VOROSHILov TALKS
ABOUT WAR

"Imperialism" Accused
Of Dark Designs On
Soviet Russia

MOSCOW AVOWS DESIRE
TO PURSUE PEACE

MOSCOW, Feb. 22.—The imperialists are making their preparations for war against the Soviet Union under cover of false phrasesology as regards striving for peace and disarmament, even while the destruction of lives and property in the Far East continues," avows M. Voroshilov, Soviet Commissar for War, in an order issued on the 14th anniversary of the formation of the Red Army.

He adds his belief that East and West are elaborating plans for intervention in Russia and social opinion is being worked up while bands of White Guards are organizing to fight the Soviet and seize Soviet interests in the Far East. Nevertheless the Soviet would persist in its pursuit of peace.—Reuter.

Challenge To Capitalism

MOSCOW, Feb. 22.—Defiance was hurled at the capitalist world to-day in a manifesto issued on the occasion of the 14th anniversary of the Red Army, by the Revolutionary War Council and signed by Comrade Voroshilov, Commissary of War.

After exhorting both the army and the civil populace to be prepared for all emergencies, the manifesto scores the imperialist Powers, insisting that they are feverishly preparing for a new war, while camouflaging their preparations with empty words about peace and disarmament. "The so-called disarmament conference," the manifesto states, opened to the accompaniment of the boom of cannon on the Pacific seaboard. While, from the rostrum of the conference, the spokesmen of the imperialist Powers talked with their tongues in their cheeks about peace in the Far East, bombs were raining there on a defenceless population, towns were being destroyed by all the implements of modern war and economic life was completely paralyzed, while thousands of toilers and their families perished miserably.

The imperialists, the manifesto goes on to charge, are preparing a new war against Soviet Russia. Under a barrage of lies, slander and misrepresentation, plans are being perfected, both in the West and in the East, for a crusade against Soviet Russia. Bands of White Russians are being organized, with the support of various Powers, to act as the vanguard of intervention and are now openly preparing for a campaign to seize the Maritime Provinces."

In conclusion, the manifesto states that the policy of the Soviet Union always has been, and always will be, one of peace. "At the same time, however, it behoves us to remain on guard. The disarmament conference notwithstanding, the international situation now, more than ever, is fraught with ominous possibilities. The war Japan is waging upon China is the best proof of that. The Red Army will protect the Soviet Union in any and all circumstances. It will beat back all our enemies, no matter how many there will be and no matter from where they will launch their attack."—Transocean—Kuo Min.

莫斯科，2月22日电——苏联战争人民委员伏罗希洛夫先生（M. Voroshilov）在红军成立14周年之际发布的一道命令中承认：“尽管远东地区的生命和财产仍在遭受破坏，但帝国主义者正披着追求和平与裁军的虚假辞藻外衣，加紧准备对苏联发动战争。”

他补充说，他相信东方和西方正在制定干涉俄罗斯的计划的计划，社会舆论正被煽动，同时白卫军团伙正在组织起来对抗苏维埃，并夺取苏维埃在远东的利益。尽管如此，苏联仍将坚持追求和平。——路透社。

对资本主义的挑战

莫斯科，2月22日电——今天，革命军事委员会在红军成立14周年之际发表了一份由战争委员伏罗希洛夫同志签署的宣言，向资本主义世界发出了挑战。

在敦促军队和民众做好应对各种紧急情况的准备后，该宣言严厉谴责了帝国主义列强，坚称它们正狂热地准备一场新的战争，同时用关于和平与裁军的空话掩盖其准备工作。宣言称：“所谓的裁军会议”是在太平洋沿岸炮声隆隆的背景下开幕的。当帝国主义列强的发言人在会议讲台上口是心非地谈论远东和平时，炸弹却如雨点般落在手无寸铁的平民身上，城镇被现代战争的所有武器摧毁，经济生活完全瘫痪，成千上万的劳动者及其家属悲惨地死去。

宣言接着指控说，帝国主义者正准备对苏维埃俄罗斯发动新的战争。在谎言、诽谤和歪曲事实的炮火掩护下，西方和东方都在完善针对苏维埃俄罗斯的十字军东征计划。在各列强的支持下，白俄团伙正在组建，作为干涉的先头部队，并公开准备开展夺取滨海省的运动。”

最后，宣言指出，苏联的政策过去是、将来也永远是和平政策。“然而，与此同时，我们必须保持警惕。尽管有裁军会议，但目前的国际局势比以往任何时候都充满了不祥的可能性。日本对中国进行的战争就是最好的证明。红军将在任何情况下保卫苏联。它将击退我们所有的敌人，无论他们有多少，也无论他们从哪里发动攻击。”——跨洋通讯社（Transocean）—《国民新闻》（Kuo Min）。
